hero.summary: Main bottleneck: translating dense GMAT wording into the correct formula, ratio, or relationship. Recognition—not basic arithmetic—is the current priority.

bottleneck.title: Main bottleneck: translating words into math
bottleneck.summary: The formula is often known once the topic is recognized, but dense wording can hide the structure. Separate recognition from calculation and translate before solving.
drill: Read one GMAT sentence and ignore the numbers initially.
Identify the hidden structure and translate it into a formula or ratio.
Progress from formula-only to formula-and-solve, then untitled problems.
Build toward timed recognition in about 10–20 seconds.

recommendations.title: Daily Translation Drill — 15–20 minutes
recommendations.detail: Ignore numbers first, identify the hidden structure, translate it into a formula or ratio, and only then solve. Build toward recognition in about 10–20 seconds.

recommendations.title: Mixed-topic Data Sufficiency
recommendations.detail: Test statement (1), then statement (2), and combine only when both are insufficient. For Yes/No questions, definite Yes or definite No is sufficient.

recommendations.title: Prove insufficiency with two cases
recommendations.detail: Find two valid cases that produce different answers; watch less than, greater than, at least, at most, exactly, and percentage boundaries.

recommendations.title: Weighted-average DS transfer
recommendations.detail: Vary the unknown and practice recognizing when multiple groups contribute to one overall average.

recommendations.title: Work-rate and proportionality DS
recommendations.detail: Translate wording first, write the rate or k-equation, and ask whether the statement determines the required constant or relationship.

recommendations.title: Untitled authentic GMAT prompts
recommendations.detail: Use medium and medium-hard problems with plausible distractors; do not name the topic before solving.
